chunks: Whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. Surely God is all-sufficing, worthy of praise.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that God is Al-Ghani Al-Hamid?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Al-Hajj, this verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over the cosmos, serving as a foundation for the call to pilgrimage (Hajj) as an act of submission to the Owner of all realms. Shia exegesis highlights the transition from 'Al-Ghani' (The Self-Sufficient) to 'Al-Hamid' (The Praiseworthy) to illustrate that while God needs nothing, He is the ultimate source of all merit and praise, inviting believers to recognize their dependence amidst divine abundance.
